body:
Nice catch. I can quibble about how to interpret the current spec text, but I think it's clear enough that this is just confusing, and we should explicitly call out the cases of same filename or same file, and state what to do.

Edge seems to follow Chromium and WebKit in this regard. (Although it doesn't fire input events.) So by default I'd think we should align the spec with 3/4 browsers.

But you seem to prefer the 1/4 behavior. I guess that makes sense especially for the renamed file case, where not getting any event is pretty bad.

Thoughts from @tkent-google @cdumez @dstorey on whether Blink/WebKit/EdgeHTML would be willing to change to always firing the change event?
I think it's reasonable to change the Blink behavior.

Have discussed with the brain-trust here, and we don't think changing the behavior from the 3/4 browser behavior is a good idea. 

First, precedent. We compared this scenario to how the `<select>` element works, since the pop-up on user selection could be compared to how the file upload selection dialog might effectively behave. On 4/4 browsers, selecting the same option multiple times does not result in a change event. Checked the same thing on input[date], with the same results. Since this matches the file-upload behavior, it seems like good precedent.

Semantically, we think the 'change' event should really only fire when there is a semantic change in the contents. For re-selecting the same thing, we don't think developers would want to re-run all their code just to get the same result.

There's also an interop risk here, although pretty small (given 3/4 browsers w/same behavior).

We would like to see the spec clarified, as it seems to imply that both 'input' and 'change' fire for any activation behavior. Seems as if the last-selected state needs to be tracked in order to have a basis for not firing 'change'. This should be clarified across the variety of input-related elements :-)

Our 2c.

Thanks very much for consulting internally, Travis. However, there's a strange subtlety here in @kosamari's post that I didn't see you discussing, which is that current 3/4 file-upload behavior seems to be based entirely on *filenames*, not files. That is,

- In 3/4 browsers, uploading two different files with the same file name will _not_ fire a change/input event---even though semantically, it seems like a change.
- In 3/4 browsers, uploading the same file twice, with two different file names (i.e. by moving or renaming it) _will_ fire a change/input event---even though semantically, the file has not changed. (Especially strange given that the web application does not have access to the file path anyway.)

So I see three options:

- 3/4 browser behavior: compare file names only
- 1/4 browser behavior: always fire a change event
- 0/4 browser behavior: compare file identity

The 0/4 behavior might be the most sensible, and fit with what you all were saying:

> Semantically, we think the 'change' event should really only fire when there is a semantic change in the contents. For re-selecting the same thing, we don't think developers would want to re-run all their code just to get the same result.

But I thought the 1/4 behavior would be a good compromise that's less complex to implement.

In any case, I definitely agree the spec needs clarification, whether toward the 3/4, 1/4, or 0/4 behavior. Just trying to figure out which direction.

I'm not sure if I should open a new issue but I'd like to ask a similar question. What is the difference between the `input` and the `change` events for file inputs? It seems that at the moment, both are fired at the same time. At least in Firefox and Chromium.

The way I interpret the first paragraph of [§ 4.10.5.5](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#common-input-element-events) is that in the case of file inputs the `input` event should be fired immediately after the user is done selecting a file, while the `change` event is fired after the file is read and sort of committed. The file selection steps are not clear on this either:

> To update the file selection for an element element:
> 
>
> 1. [Queue an element task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#queue-an-element-task) on the [user interaction task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#user-interaction-task-source) given element and the following steps:

> 
>
> 1. Update element's [selected files](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-type-file-selected) so that it represents the user's selection.
> 
> 2. [Fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named [input](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) element, with the [bubbles](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles) and [composed](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-composed) attributes initialized to true.
> 
> 3. [Fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named [change](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/indices.html#event-change) at the [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) element, with the [bubbles](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-bubbles) attribute initialized to true.

Is my interpretation valid? Is it a flaw in user agent implementations or an ambiguity in the Living Standard?
